aspects.says: Double-checked locking's first check reads without the lock, so without a volatile field a caller can get a reference to an object whose constructor's writes it doesn't see.
basis: section:Double-Checked Locking Reads Without the Lock, So Its Field Must Be volatile

aspects.says: The check under the lock is what stops a second caller that also found the field empty from creating the object again.
basis: section:Double-Checked Locking Reads Without the Lock, So Its Field Must Be volatile

aspects.says: A lock on a different object neither excludes the writer nor gives an edge to its writes, even when both methods are synchronized.
basis: section:A Lock on a Different Object Gives No Edge

aspects.says: A holder class's static final field is created on the first use of the holder, under the JVM's class initialization lock, so it needs no volatile and no check.
basis: section:Double-Checked Locking Reads Without the Lock, So Its Field Must Be volatile
aspects.reason: class initialization runs once per class loader, so a graded test can't start it again per case, and an eager static field passes any check of the result; the page shows the run

aspects.says: Every Lock implementation gives the same memory effects as a monitor; a failed tryLock is not required to give any.
basis: section:Releasing a Lock Publishes Every Write Made Before It, to the Next Thread That Takes the Same Lock
aspects.reason: a javadoc guarantee; explicit locks are practised in unit 6.3.x, and a missing edge can't be shown by a deterministic test

aspects.says: A synchronized instance method locks the object and a static synchronized method locks the Class object, so the two give no edge to each other over a static field.
basis: section:A Lock on a Different Object Gives No Edge

aspects.says: An unlock of a monitor happens-before every later lock of the same monitor, so a reader that takes the writer's lock sees every write the writer made before releasing it, inside the block or earlier; a reader that takes no lock is promised nothing.
basis: section:Releasing a Lock Publishes Every Write Made Before It, to the Next Thread That Takes the Same Lock

aspects.says: A reader that skips the lock can run between a locked writer's writes and see two fields that were never written together; reading under the same lock prevents it.
basis: section:A Reader That Skips the Lock Can See Two Fields That Were Never Written Together
section:Spot the Problem: the Price Book

aspects.says: A lock on an object no other thread can reach orders nothing, and the JIT may remove it along with any ordering the code relied on.
basis: section:A Lock on a Different Object Gives No Edge
aspects.reason: whether the JIT removes the lock depends on compilation and JVM flags; a graded test can't make it happen on demand, so the page shows the run instead
